correctness.rationale: For any length, cyclic factors are FO2-definable by alternating reuse of x,y; the common factor language determines the primitive necklace by periodic-prefix pigeonholing. Multiplicities k below 4 (period1), 3 (period2) and 2 (period>=3) are distinguished by explicit existential FO2 unary-pattern or nonadjacency formulas. For k at/above the appropriate bound, residue-preserving matching atomic two-types form a two-pebble back-and-forth system: the possible relations to a fixed pebble include equality, both directed neighbors, and nonneighbors exactly as counted in the proof. This gives full FO2 equivalence for arbitrary quantifier rank, including self-loop length1 and bidirected length2 boundaries. A finite independent type-refinement test passed 153 binary and 225 ternary cyclic words (140 and 219 equivalence classes respectively), but is only corroborative.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-quantifier-depth semantic classification of a natural infinite family of finite colored directed cycles, including sharp distinct stabilization cutoffs at primitive periods 1, 2 and >=3. It isolates an exact expressive-power boundary of the 2-variable restriction and yields a linear-time equivalence decision using primitive periods and canonical rotations, not just a routine instance check.
